content: Hydralazine is a medication prescribed to treat high blood pressure. It functions by relaxing the blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily throughout the body. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Hydralazine is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically administered two to four times daily at evenly spaced intervals. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take hydralazine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. While hydralazine helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure the condition. Continue taking hydralazine even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Hydralazine is also used in the management of conditions such as congestive heart failure and after heart valve replacement surgery. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your specific condition with your doctor. Before taking hydralazine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to hydralazine, aspirin, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some processed foods and medications), or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially indomethacin (Indocin), metoprolol (Lopressor), propranolol (Inderal), and any vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had coronary artery disease, rheumatic heart disease, kidney or liver disease, or a history of heart attack. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking hydralazine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking hydralazine. Additionally, ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while on this medication, as alcohol can exacerbate the side effects of hydralazine. Take hydralazine with meals or a snack. Your doctor may recommend a low-salt or low-sodium diet; follow these dietary instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of hydralazine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Hydralazine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they persist or worsen: flushing (a sensation of warmth), headache, upset stomach, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhea, constipation, eye tearing, stuffy nose, or rash. If you experience severe side effects such as fainting, joint or muscle pain, unexplained fever, rapid heartbeat, chest pain, swollen ankles or feet, or numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store hydralazine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Regular monitoring of your blood pressure is necessary to evaluate your response to hydralazine. Your doctor may ask you to check your blood pressure daily; ask your doctor or pharmacist for instructions on how to do this. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
